transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (CTO, Springboard), Rosa Martinez (Cloud Eng), Evan Li (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): High-level kickoff for implementation and staging. Action items around security docs, VPC peering, and perf runs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood. Priya and I are here to walk through the onboarding accelerator today, quick agenda: security, network, pilot scope, and next steps. how's that sound?
[00:18] Jordan Blake: sounds good. quick note, i'm on east coast so apologies if i pop in late, i'm based in nyc.
[00:25] Rosa Martinez: Rosa here, i'll be owning the VPC peering and infra side.
[00:29] Evan Li: and Evan, PM — i'll own the success / acceptance criteria.
[00:33] Priya Nair: great — we'll start with a short runbook walkthrough then deep dive into connectivity.

[01:00] Alex Chen: so first question is, are you planning to use Redwood hosted API for the pilot or try Dedicated right away? any blockers like data residency or on‑prem?
[01:15] Jordan Blake: prefer hosted for speed, but we have strict data governance for PII pipelines; may want VPC peering or Private later. timeline is pretty tight — product leadership wants a pilot in 3 weeks.
[01:30] Evan Li: goal is end‑to‑end feature demo with 95th percentile latency under 350ms for short queries, and cost below our internal budget.
[01:40] Priya Nair: ok that helps. quick clarifying question — when you say 350ms is that token latency or end‑to‑end?
[01:47] Evan Li: we're measuring end‑to‑end from request to first token.

[02:10] Rosa Martinez: for the VPC, we'll need peering. can you outline what info you need? e.g. peering CIDR, SAML metadata for SSO?
[02:20] Alex Chen: yes — we'll need SSO/SAML metadata for SCIM, VPC CIDR for peering, and a list of allowed egress IPs. also mention if you plan to use customer KMS.
[02:35] Rosa Martinez: yes, KMS integration for encrypting logs is required.

[03:10] Priya Nair: on the infra side, if you go Hosted with VPC peering we still maintain control plane, but traffic sits in your VPC via peering; Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable throughput. tradeoffs are cost vs SLA.
[03:28] Jordan Blake: what's the delta in cost for Dedicated? ballpark.
[03:32] Alex Chen: depends on throughput but typically Dedicated is 2–3x hosted at baseline if you reserve GPUs, but you get a hard SLO, burst capability, and no noisy neighbor. for a short pilot we can stage on hosted then move to Dedicated if throughput needs justify it.

[04:05] Evan Li: hold on — we saw an internal note about kernel optimization in Redwood's docs, is that part of the setup? our infra lead mentioned something about "compiling kernels".
[04:15] Priya Nair: yes, that's kernel selection and quantization profiles; it's internal to the runtime. we'll recommend a profile for your model mix. we can toggle quantization to reduce cost, but it can affect quality a little.

[04:50] Rosa Martinez: any compliance docs we can share with security? SOC‑2, ISO?
[04:55] Alex Chen: yes — we'll share SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest/in transit details, and KMS integration docs. i'll attach them after the call.

[05:25] Jordan Blake: logging/observability: we need audit logs for token access and admin actions for our compliance team. how granular are those?
[05:35] Priya Nair: Console exposes per‑token cost metrics and token latency, plus audit trails for admin changes. logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 depending on setup.

[06:05] Evan Li: also curious about model rollouts — can we canary a new model and fallback automatically?
[06:13] Alex Chen: yes, rollouts with automatic fallback policies are supported; you can define traffic split and automatic rollback triggers for regressions.

[06:45] Rosa Martinez: networking question: is peering bi‑directional? and are there any NAT issues we should watch for?
[06:52] Priya Nair: peering is bi‑directional; we recommend routing only necessary subnets, and ensure no overlapping CIDRs. NAT can be used for egress rules but it's usually simpler to provide allowed egress range.

[07:20] Jordan Blake: timeline check: pilot in 3 weeks — is that realistic with peering and security review?
[07:29] Alex Chen: it's tight but doable. immediate priority is: we share runbook + security pack today, you share VPC and SSO details ASAP, and Priya will run a perf baseline once prompts are in.

[08:05] Evan Li: about prompts — we'll send 8–10 canonical prompts plus worst‑case long context examples. will that be enough?
[08:12] Priya Nair: yes, that helps. also include expected success criteria per prompt — e.g., F1 or exact matches for certain tasks.

[08:40] Rosa Martinez: one thing — do you keep KV cache or prefix cache? our engineers referred to "kv cash" and we want to understand caching behavior for session state.
[08:52] Priya Nair: yep, we use KV cache for autoregressive models; we'll document typical cache hit rates and options to evict or persist. sometimes the transcript might say K‑V cash, haha.

[09:25] Alex Chen: ok moving on, any concerns with SSO/SAML? Jordan?
[09:30] Jordan Blake: security team prefers IdP initiated SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. also want role based access controls mapped to our org roles.
[09:40] Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML SSO + SCIM; RBAC roles are configurable — we'll include a mapping template.

[10:05] Evan Li: for cost tracking — can we tag requests or teams?
[10:12] Alex Chen: yes, Console supports per‑token tagging and per‑route cost breakdowns. we'll show examples in the runbook.

[10:40] Rosa Martinez: what about private deployment / on prem later?
[10:45] Alex Chen: we offer Private deployment with a customer control plane; longer lead time and separate contract, but possible after pilot.

[11:10] Jordan Blake: ok, can we do a short blast demo of the API and a sample inference? get a feel for latency.
[11:16] Priya Nair: sure — i'll share a quick curl example now and then we can schedule a hands‑on session.
[11:30] [screen share / link shared] Priya Nair: (demonstrates an example request) here's a simple prompt, sending to the hosted endpoint, you can see the token stream.

[12:05] Evan Li: seen. curious how streaming interacts with our client SDK. will there be a JS SDK?
[12:12] Alex Chen: yes, SDKs available in JS and Python with streaming primitives. we'll include code samples.

[12:40] Rosa Martinez: about data retention — do you persist logs? for our regulated flows we need short retention and deletion on request.
[12:48] Alex Chen: retention is configurable; we support deletion requests and can shorten retention for pilot data. we'll provide the deletion SLA.

[13:15] Jordan Blake: ok we also want to do a light load test during staging — what does that look like?
[13:22] Priya Nair: typical staging load test is synthetic traffic that mimics your prompt distribution; we'll run 1k qps synthetic for a short window to validate autoscaling and KV cache behavior. for Dedicated we size GPUs accordingly.

[13:55] Evan Li: can Redwood instruments collect per‑route tail latency histograms?
[14:00] Priya Nair: yep, Console has histograms and per‑route breakdowns, and you can route certain traffic to lower‑cost fallback models automatically.

[14:30] Rosa Martinez: any gotchas on IP whitelisting?
[14:34] Alex Chen: we'll supply a small set of egress IPs; if you have strict whitelists we can provide a CIDR block list.

[15:00] Jordan Blake: ok timeline recap please.
[15:05] Alex Chen: recap: Alex will send runbook and security docs today; Rosa sends VPC + SSO metadata by 2026‑11‑06; Evan sends prompts and success criteria by 2026‑11‑08; Priya runs perf baseline and we reconvene for sizing workshop w/ Jordan by 2026‑11‑11.

[15:30] Evan Li: sounds good. any specific metrics we should record during baseline?
[15:35] Priya Nair: please capture 95th percentile latency, first‑token time, token throughput, and model quality metrics per prompt set. also note context lengths.

[16:05] Rosa Martinez: small question — are there any integration points for our SRE pager? we want alerts for degraded latency.
[16:13] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood's Console can forward alerts to PagerDuty or Slack. we'll include recommended thresholds.

[16:45] Jordan Blake: what's the support window during pilot?
[16:50] Alex Chen: we'll provide standard business hours support and an oncall SE for critical issues during the pilot. with Dedicated we can add a premium SLA.

[17:10] Evan Li: good. any competitor concerns? we've seen other vendors push simpler pricing but less observability.
[17:18] Alex Chen: noted — we'll emphasize observability and cost tooling in the runbook.

[17:40] Rosa Martinez: ok final — can you send the runbook and a checklist we can pass to our security review?
[17:46] Alex Chen: yes — i'll send the runbook, security pack, and a checklist after the call.

[17:58] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and lock in the sizing workshop; any last Qs?
[18:05] Jordan Blake: no, thanks — excited to get started.
[18:08] Evan Li: thanks all.
[18:10] Rosa Martinez: thanks, bye.

Keywords/Notes: canary rollouts, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K V cash), SSO/SCIM, VPC peering, Dedicated capacity, runbook share, perf baseline, SOC2, KMS integration.
